# Tricorn (mathematics)

- [Ελληνικά](https://el.wikipedia.org/wiki/%CE%A4%CF%81%CE%B9%CE%BA%CE%AD%CF%81%CE%B1%CF%84%CE%BF_(%CE%BC%CE%B1%CE%B8%CE%B7%CE%BC%CE%B1%CF%84%CE%B9%CE%BA%CE%AC))
- [Español](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tricornio_(matem%C3%A1ticas))
 [Edit links](https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Special:EntityPage/Q7841294#sitelinks-wikipedia)                          From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia   Mandelbar Set [![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/00/Mandelbar_20210819.png/250px-Mandelbar_20210819.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Mandelbar_20210819.png)A tricorn, created on a computer in Kalles Fraktaler. [![tricornZoom](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1b/TricornSmallZoom.gif/250px-TricornSmallZoom.gif?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:TricornSmallZoom.gif)Tricorn zoom onto mini-tricorn [![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d0/Multibar.gif/250px-Multibar.gif?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Multibar.gif)Multicorns with the power going from 1 to 5

In [mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathematics), the **tricorn**, sometimes called the **Mandelbar set**, is a [fractal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fractal) defined in a similar way to the [Mandelbrot set](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mandelbrot_set), but using the mapping     z ↦     z ¯     2   + c   {\displaystyle z\mapsto {\bar {z}}^{2}+c}   instead of     z ↦  z  2   + c   {\displaystyle z\mapsto z^{2}+c}   used for the Mandelbrot set. It was introduced by W. D. Crowe, R. Hasson, P. J. Rippon, and P. E. D. Strain-Clark.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tricorn_(mathematics)#cite_note-1) [John Milnor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Milnor) found tricorn-like sets as a prototypical configuration in the parameter space of real cubic polynomials, and in various other families of rational maps.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tricorn_(mathematics)#cite_note-2)

The characteristic [three-cornered shape](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deltoid_curve) created by this fractal repeats with variations at different scales, showing the same sort of [self-similarity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Self-similarity) as the Mandelbrot set. In addition to smaller tricorns, smaller versions of the Mandelbrot set are also contained within the tricorn fractal.

A more general form of the Tricorn fractal are **Multicorn Fractals**. These are defined similarly to the Tricorn fractal, but instead of squaring the complex conjugate of *z*, we raise it to any positive integer degree, *d*:

## Formal definition

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Tricorn_(mathematics)&action=edit&section=1)]

The tricorn     T   {\displaystyle T}   is defined by a family of quadratic [antiholomorphic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antiholomorphic_function) [polynomials](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polynomial)

      f  c   :  C  →  C    {\displaystyle f_{c}:\mathbb {C} \to \mathbb {C} }

given by

      f  c   : z ↦     z ¯     2   + c ,   {\displaystyle f_{c}:z\mapsto {\bar {z}}^{2}+c,}

where     c   {\displaystyle c}   is a complex parameter. For each     c   {\displaystyle c}  , one looks at the forward orbit

     ( 0 ,  f  c   ( 0 ) ,  f  c   (  f  c   ( 0 ) ) ,  f  c   (  f  c   (  f  c   ( 0 ) ) ) , … )   {\displaystyle (0,f_{c}(0),f_{c}(f_{c}(0)),f_{c}(f_{c}(f_{c}(0))),\ldots )}

of the [critical point](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Critical_point_(mathematics))     0   {\displaystyle 0}   of the antiholomorphic polynomial      p  c     {\displaystyle p_{c}}  . In analogy with the [Mandelbrot set](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mandelbrot_set), the tricorn is defined as the set of all parameters     c   {\displaystyle c}   for which the forward orbit of the critical point is bounded. This is equivalent to saying that the tricorn is the connectedness locus of the family of quadratic antiholomorphic polynomials; i.e. the set of all parameters     c   {\displaystyle c}   for which the [Julia set](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julia_set)     J (  f  c   )   {\displaystyle J(f_{c})}   is connected.

The higher degree analogues of the tricorn are known as the multicorns.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tricorn_(mathematics)#cite_note-auto-3) These are the connectedness loci of the family of antiholomorphic polynomials      f  c   : z ↦     z ¯     d   + c   {\displaystyle f_{c}:z\mapsto {\bar {z}}^{d}+c}  .

## Basic properties

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Tricorn_(mathematics)&action=edit&section=2)]
- The tricorn is [compact](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Compact_space), and [connected](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Connectedness).[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tricorn_(mathematics)#cite_note-4) In fact, Nakane modified [Douady](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adrien_Douady) and [Hubbard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_H._Hubbard)'s proof of the connectedness of the [Mandelbrot set](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mandelbrot_set) to construct a dynamically defined [real-analytic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Analytic_function) [diffeomorphism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diffeomorphism) from the exterior of the tricorn onto the exterior of the [closed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Closed_set) [unit disc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unit_disk) in the [complex plane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Complex_plane). One can define [external parameter rays](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/External_ray) of the tricorn as the inverse images of [radial lines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radial_line) under this diffeomorphism.
- Every hyperbolic component of the tricorn is [simply connected](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simply_connected_space).[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tricorn_(mathematics)#cite_note-auto-3)
- The boundary of every hyperbolic component of odd period of the tricorn contains real-analytic arcs consisting of quasi-conformally equivalent but conformally distinct parabolic parameters.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tricorn_(mathematics)#cite_note-cornell.edu-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tricorn_(mathematics)#cite_note-auto1-6) Such an arc is called a parabolic arc of the tricorn. This is in stark contrast with the corresponding situation for the Mandelbrot set, where parabolic parameters of a given period are known to be isolated.
- The boundary of every odd period hyperbolic component consists only of parabolic parameters. More precisely, the boundary of every hyperbolic component of odd period of the tricorn is a simple closed curve consisting of exactly three parabolic cusp points as well as three parabolic arcs, each connecting two parabolic cusps.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tricorn_(mathematics)#cite_note-auto1-6)
- Every parabolic arc of period k intersects the boundary of a hyperbolic component of period 2k along an arc consisting of the set of parameters where the parabolic fixed point index is at least 1. In particular, every parabolic arc has, at both ends, an interval of positive length at which bifurcation from a hyperbolic component of odd period k to a hyperbolic component of period 2k occurs.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tricorn_(mathematics)#cite_note-7)

Much like the [Mandelbrot set](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mandelbrot_set), the tricorn has many complex and intricate designs. Due to their similarity, they share many features. However, in the tricorn such features appear to be squeezed and stretched along its boundary.

The following images are progressional zooms on a selected     c   {\displaystyle c}   value where     c = 0.48 + 0.58 i   {\displaystyle c=0.48+0.58i}  . The images are not stretched or altered, that is how they look on magnification.

## Implementation

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Tricorn_(mathematics)&action=edit&section=4)]

The below pseudocode implementation hardcodes the complex operations for Z. Consider implementing [complex number](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Complex_number) operations to allow for more dynamic and reusable code.

```
For each pixel (x, y) on the screen, do:
{
    x = scaled x coordinate of pixel (scaled to lie in the Mandelbrot X scale (-2.5, 1))
    y = scaled y coordinate of pixel (scaled to lie in the Mandelbrot Y scale (-1, 1))

    zx = x;  // zx represents the real part of z
    zy = y;  // zy represents the imaginary part of z

    iteration = 0
    max_iteration = 1000

    while (zx * zx + zy * zy ≤ 4 and iteration < max_iteration)
    {
        xtemp = zx * zx - zy * zy + x
        zy = -2 * zx * zy + y
        zx = xtemp
        iteration = iteration + 1
    }

    if (iteration == max_iteration)  // Belongs to the set
        return inside_color;

    return iteration * color; 15
}
```

## Further topological properties

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Tricorn_(mathematics)&action=edit&section=5)]

The tricorn is not path connected.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tricorn_(mathematics)#cite_note-cornell.edu-5) Hubbard and Schleicher showed that there are hyperbolic components of odd period of the tricorn that cannot be connected to the hyperbolic component of period one by paths. A stronger statement to the effect that no two (non-real) odd period hyperbolic components of the tricorn can be connected by a path was proved by Inou and Mukherjee.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tricorn_(mathematics)#cite_note-auto2-8)

It is well known that every rational parameter ray of the Mandelbrot set lands at a single parameter.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tricorn_(mathematics)#cite_note-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tricorn_(mathematics)#cite_note-10) On the other hand, the rational parameter rays at odd-periodic (except period one) angles of the tricorn accumulate on arcs of positive length consisting of parabolic parameters.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tricorn_(mathematics)#cite_note-11) Moreover, unlike the Mandelbrot set, the dynamically natural straightening map from a baby tricorn to the original tricorn is discontinuous at infinitely many parameters.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tricorn_(mathematics)#cite_note-auto2-8)

Tricorn (mathematics)

# Tricorn (mathematics)

- [Ελληνικά](https://el.wikipedia.org/wiki/%CE%A4%CF%81%CE%B9%CE%BA%CE%AD%CF%81%CE%B1%CF%84%CE%BF_(%CE%BC%CE%B1%CE%B8%CE%B7%CE%BC%CE%B1%CF%84%CE%B9%CE%BA%CE%AC))
- [Español](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tricornio_(matem%C3%A1ticas))
 [Edit links](https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Special:EntityPage/Q7841294#sitelinks-wikipedia)                          From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia   Mandelbar Set [![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/00/Mandelbar_20210819.png/250px-Mandelbar_20210819.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Mandelbar_20210819.png)A tricorn, created on a computer in Kalles Fraktaler. [![tricornZoom](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1b/TricornSmallZoom.gif/250px-TricornSmallZoom.gif?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:TricornSmallZoom.gif)Tricorn zoom onto mini-tricorn [![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d0/Multibar.gif/250px-Multibar.gif?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Multibar.gif)Multicorns with the power going from 1 to 5

In [mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathematics), the **tricorn**, sometimes called the **Mandelbar set**, is a [fractal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fractal) defined in a similar way to the [Mandelbrot set](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mandelbrot_set), but using the mapping     z ↦     z ¯     2   + c   {\displaystyle z\mapsto {\bar {z}}^{2}+c}   instead of     z ↦  z  2   + c   {\displaystyle z\mapsto z^{2}+c}   used for the Mandelbrot set. It was introduced by W. D. Crowe, R. Hasson, P. J. Rippon, and P. E. D. Strain-Clark.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tricorn_(mathematics)#cite_note-1) [John Milnor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Milnor) found tricorn-like sets as a prototypical configuration in the parameter space of real cubic polynomials, and in various other families of rational maps.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tricorn_(mathematics)#cite_note-2)

The characteristic [three-cornered shape](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deltoid_curve) created by this fractal repeats with variations at different scales, showing the same sort of [self-similarity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Self-similarity) as the Mandelbrot set. In addition to smaller tricorns, smaller versions of the Mandelbrot set are also contained within the tricorn fractal.

A more general form of the Tricorn fractal are **Multicorn Fractals**. These are defined similarly to the Tricorn fractal, but instead of squaring the complex conjugate of *z*, we raise it to any positive integer degree, *d*:

Formal definition

# Formal definition

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Tricorn_(mathematics)&action=edit&section=1)]

The tricorn     T   {\displaystyle T}   is defined by a family of quadratic [antiholomorphic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antiholomorphic_function) [polynomials](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polynomial)

      f  c   :  C  →  C    {\displaystyle f_{c}:\mathbb {C} \to \mathbb {C} }

given by

      f  c   : z ↦     z ¯     2   + c ,   {\displaystyle f_{c}:z\mapsto {\bar {z}}^{2}+c,}

where     c   {\displaystyle c}   is a complex parameter. For each     c   {\displaystyle c}  , one looks at the forward orbit

     ( 0 ,  f  c   ( 0 ) ,  f  c   (  f  c   ( 0 ) ) ,  f  c   (  f  c   (  f  c   ( 0 ) ) ) , … )   {\displaystyle (0,f_{c}(0),f_{c}(f_{c}(0)),f_{c}(f_{c}(f_{c}(0))),\ldots )}

of the [critical point](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Critical_point_(mathematics))     0   {\displaystyle 0}   of the antiholomorphic polynomial      p  c     {\displaystyle p_{c}}  . In analogy with the [Mandelbrot set](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mandelbrot_set), the tricorn is defined as the set of all parameters     c   {\displaystyle c}   for which the forward orbit of the critical point is bounded. This is equivalent to saying that the tricorn is the connectedness locus of the family of quadratic antiholomorphic polynomials; i.e. the set of all parameters     c   {\displaystyle c}   for which the [Julia set](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julia_set)     J (  f  c   )   {\displaystyle J(f_{c})}   is connected.

The higher degree analogues of the tricorn are known as the multicorns.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tricorn_(mathematics)#cite_note-auto-3) These are the connectedness loci of the family of antiholomorphic polynomials      f  c   : z ↦     z ¯     d   + c   {\displaystyle f_{c}:z\mapsto {\bar {z}}^{d}+c}  .

Basic properties

# Basic properties

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Tricorn_(mathematics)&action=edit&section=2)]
- The tricorn is [compact](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Compact_space), and [connected](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Connectedness).[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tricorn_(mathematics)#cite_note-4) In fact, Nakane modified [Douady](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adrien_Douady) and [Hubbard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_H._Hubbard)'s proof of the connectedness of the [Mandelbrot set](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mandelbrot_set) to construct a dynamically defined [real-analytic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Analytic_function) [diffeomorphism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diffeomorphism) from the exterior of the tricorn onto the exterior of the [closed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Closed_set) [unit disc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unit_disk) in the [complex plane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Complex_plane). One can define [external parameter rays](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/External_ray) of the tricorn as the inverse images of [radial lines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radial_line) under this diffeomorphism.
- Every hyperbolic component of the tricorn is [simply connected](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simply_connected_space).[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tricorn_(mathematics)#cite_note-auto-3)
- The boundary of every hyperbolic component of odd period of the tricorn contains real-analytic arcs consisting of quasi-conformally equivalent but conformally distinct parabolic parameters.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tricorn_(mathematics)#cite_note-cornell.edu-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tricorn_(mathematics)#cite_note-auto1-6) Such an arc is called a parabolic arc of the tricorn. This is in stark contrast with the corresponding situation for the Mandelbrot set, where parabolic parameters of a given period are known to be isolated.
- The boundary of every odd period hyperbolic component consists only of parabolic parameters. More precisely, the boundary of every hyperbolic component of odd period of the tricorn is a simple closed curve consisting of exactly three parabolic cusp points as well as three parabolic arcs, each connecting two parabolic cusps.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tricorn_(mathematics)#cite_note-auto1-6)
- Every parabolic arc of period k intersects the boundary of a hyperbolic component of period 2k along an arc consisting of the set of parameters where the parabolic fixed point index is at least 1. In particular, every parabolic arc has, at both ends, an interval of positive length at which bifurcation from a hyperbolic component of odd period k to a hyperbolic component of period 2k occurs.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tricorn_(mathematics)#cite_note-7)

Much like the [Mandelbrot set](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mandelbrot_set), the tricorn has many complex and intricate designs. Due to their similarity, they share many features. However, in the tricorn such features appear to be squeezed and stretched along its boundary.

Implementation

# Implementation

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Tricorn_(mathematics)&action=edit&section=4)]

The below pseudocode implementation hardcodes the complex operations for Z. Consider implementing [complex number](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Complex_number) operations to allow for more dynamic and reusable code.

```
For each pixel (x, y) on the screen, do:
{
    x = scaled x coordinate of pixel (scaled to lie in the Mandelbrot X scale (-2.5, 1))
    y = scaled y coordinate of pixel (scaled to lie in the Mandelbrot Y scale (-1, 1))

    zx = x;  // zx represents the real part of z
    zy = y;  // zy represents the imaginary part of z

    iteration = 0
    max_iteration = 1000

    while (zx * zx + zy * zy ≤ 4 and iteration < max_iteration)
    {
        xtemp = zx * zx - zy * zy + x
        zy = -2 * zx * zy + y
        zx = xtemp
        iteration = iteration + 1
    }

    if (iteration == max_iteration)  // Belongs to the set
        return inside_color;

    return iteration * color; 15
}
```

Further topological properties

# Further topological properties

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Tricorn_(mathematics)&action=edit&section=5)]

The tricorn is not path connected.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tricorn_(mathematics)#cite_note-cornell.edu-5) Hubbard and Schleicher showed that there are hyperbolic components of odd period of the tricorn that cannot be connected to the hyperbolic component of period one by paths. A stronger statement to the effect that no two (non-real) odd period hyperbolic components of the tricorn can be connected by a path was proved by Inou and Mukherjee.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tricorn_(mathematics)#cite_note-auto2-8)

It is well known that every rational parameter ray of the Mandelbrot set lands at a single parameter.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tricorn_(mathematics)#cite_note-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tricorn_(mathematics)#cite_note-10) On the other hand, the rational parameter rays at odd-periodic (except period one) angles of the tricorn accumulate on arcs of positive length consisting of parabolic parameters.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tricorn_(mathematics)#cite_note-11) Moreover, unlike the Mandelbrot set, the dynamically natural straightening map from a baby tricorn to the original tricorn is discontinuous at infinitely many parameters.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tricorn_(mathematics)#cite_note-auto2-8)
